sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Iowa, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Monday, October 19Passed

A written request for a ballot by mail had to reach your county auditor by 5 p.m. on Monday, October 19, 2026 (the same day as the voter registration deadline, 15 days before the election). That deadline has passed. You can still ask for and vote an absentee ballot in person at the county auditor's office through Monday, November 2, 2026. (the law)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be received in the county auditor's office before the polls close on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A postmark does not count; the ballot has to arrive by then. (the law)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Monday, November 2, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Iowa’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Iowa or in another state? What Iowa says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Any registered voter can vote absentee when they expect to be away from their precinct on Election Day, to be kept from the polls by illness or disability, or simply to be unable to go to the polls. The law lists no proof of a reason. (the law)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Send a written, signed request to your county auditor. You can use the state's request form or a sheet of paper (at least 3 by 5 inches) with: your name and signature and the date you signed, your date of birth, the address where you are registered, your voter verification number (Iowa driver's license or state ID number, or the four-digit PIN on your Iowa Voter ID Card), and the election you want a ballot for. It does not need to be notarized. You may ask for the ballot to be mailed to an address other than your home (the auditor then also sends a notice to that address if anything is missing from your request). (the law)
  • In person. Ask for and vote an absentee ballot at your county auditor's office (or a place the auditor names) during in-person absentee voting. You fill in a short request there, show ID, mark the ballot and hand it back on the spot. (the law)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail the sealed return envelope to your county auditor. It must arrive before the polls close on Election Day. (the law)
  • In person. Bring the sealed envelope to the county auditor's office yourself before the polls close on Election Day. Only you, someone who lives with you, or a close relative may return it for you; a voter who is blind or has a disability may name a delivery agent (one agent may return no more than two ballots). Anyone returning it for you must deliver it within 72 hours. (the law)
  • Drop box. A county may have one drop box, at the county auditor's office or on the county land right around that building. Counties do not have to have one. It closes when the polls close on Election Day. (the law)

What the envelope needs

The request must include your voter verification number: your Iowa driver's license or state ID number, or the four-digit PIN on your Iowa Voter ID Card. If you do not have it, the auditor will check who you are by asking for two facts such as your date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security number. Sign the statement on the ballot envelope. No notary is needed. (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Iowa’s own site (federal guide)

Vote early in person instead

Wednesday, October 14, 2026 to Monday, November 2, 2026.

In-person absentee voting at your county auditor's office starts no more than 20 days before the election: Wednesday, October 14, 2026, and runs through Monday, November 2, 2026 (not on Election Day). Check your county auditor for hours. (the law)

Students

At school in Iowa, away from home

Iowa law says a student who lives at or near their school, and who can also claim a home somewhere else, may choose either place as their home for voting. A person does not lose their home for voting by living for a while in another precinct. (the law)

At school in another state, with Iowa as home

Iowa law says a person does not lose their Iowa home for voting by living for a while in another state, and a student may choose either their school or their other home as their voting home. A student who registers to vote in another state gives up their Iowa voting home. An Iowa student at school in another state can keep their Iowa registration and vote absentee by mail. (the law)

Military and overseas

Military voters, their families and U.S. citizens living overseas use the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA) to register and ask for a ballot; it can be sent by mail, email or fax and needs no witness. Use a new one each year. For these voters, a mailed ballot counts if it is postmarked by Monday, November 2, 2026 and received by noon on Monday, November 9, 2026. Overseas service members may return the ballot by mail, email or fax; other overseas voters return it by mail. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is a backup if your ballot does not come in time. (the law)

Iowa in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The deadline to ask for a ballot by mail (5 p.m. Monday, October 19, 2026) has passed. You can still vote absentee in person at your county auditor's office through Monday, November 2, or vote at your polling place on Election Day.
  • Iowa law does not let a county auditor mail request forms to voters who have not asked for one.

How this was checked

  • The Iowa Secretary of State's own absentee pages (sos.iowa.gov, voterready.iowa.gov) could not be read for this record: they answered with a check for human visitors, which we do not get around. Every fact here is from the Iowa Code (2026 edition) or the federal FVAP guide; the ballot tracker's address is the one the FVAP guide gives. Check your county auditor for hours and drop box locations.
